items.title: ii. Reactions of Halogenoalkanes with KCN

source_refs.note: ii. Reactions of Halogenoalkanes with KCN: a main subheading of 21.4 Examples of Reactions of Halogenoalkanes, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 82-82.

blocks.text: Since cyanide ion (CN⁻) is a strong nucleophile but a weak base so it reacts with halogenoalkanes to give substitution product, a nitrile. The reaction is typically carried out by heating the halogenoalkane with an ethanolic solution of potassium cyanide under reflux. Bromoethane reacts with potassium cyanide to give propane nitrile.

blocks.alt: Displayed bromoethane + K+ -C(triple bond)N, with 'alcohol' over the arrow, gives displayed propanenitrile, H3C-CH2-C(triple bond)N, + KBr.
